lines: Mum, the bougainvillea has gone purple in the dusk. Very purple.
Yes, the lemon tree by the café. Biscuit sniffed it. Approved.
No, Mum, I water the basil. Biscuit only supervises.
Tomorrow? Long walk, then figs. Biscuit has signed off on it.
Grandad's geraniums? Still on my sill. Still showing off.
Biscuit says hello to Auntie. He said it with one ear.
The jasmine is out. You can smell it on the phone, nearly.
He found a petal on his nose. He is wearing it now.
Yes, Mum, I remember your lemon cake. So does Biscuit.
Plan for tomorrow: repot the mint. Biscuit will dig, I'll pot.
My sister wants a cutting from the rosemary. I said yes.
The lamps are on. The lemons look like little lamps too.
Dad always whistles at blue hour. I'm whistling now. Badly.
Saturday I'll bring you oranges. Biscuit will carry one.
He is sitting under the palm like he owns it. He might.
Remember the fig tree at Gran's? There's one here. Smaller.
Hold on, Mum. Biscuit wants to smell the lavender first.
The sky is the colour of your blue teapot. Exactly that.
Tomorrow the plan is simple. Walk, nap, walk. His plan.
The pots on the steps have new flowers. Pink ones. Many.
Yes, I wear the scarf you knitted. Biscuit likes the tassels.
A cypress, Mum. Tall, thin. Like Uncle Kemal, but greener.
I planted the tomato seeds you sent. Three are up. Tiny.
Biscuit just bowed to the hibiscus. I don't know why either.
We'll call again at breakfast. He wants to show you his stick.
The string lights just came on. Biscuit wagged at them.
Mum says the lemons look plump. I'll tell them. They know.
Yes, the bench under the bougainvillea. Our usual spot.
Your mint is on my windowsill, Mum. Thriving. Like you.
The roses by the kiosk smell of honey tonight. Promise.
I said goodnight to the basil. Biscuit said it louder.
I'll buy a bigger pot for the lemon tree. His idea.
Remember when Biscuit fit in my coat pocket? He still tries.
He's sniffing the lavender like a wine expert. Notes of lavender.
Sister, look. The fountain, the lamps, the dog. Ta-da.
Yes, Dad, the olive tree. It has two olives. Proudly.
Your geranium cutting took, Mum. It has a flower. Just one.
Plans? A cup of tea, and the garden on the balcony. Quiet ones.
I'm walking past the jasmine slowly. For you. You'd stop here.
Yes, he had his supper. Then he had Henri's supper crumb.
The light is all lavender and gold. Very you, Mum.

He's posing by the bougainvillea. Take the screenshot now.
Remember Grandad's fig jam? Odile makes one nearly as good.
The palm is waving. I'm waving back. On your behalf.
Biscuit wants to know if your cat says hello. Tell him yes.
My sister says her tulips came up. I'll tell the bougainvillea.
I found a lemon on the path. I put it back under its tree.
There's a snail on the planter. Biscuit is being very polite.
The sea is all blue now and the lamps are all yellow. Lovely.
Sunday, lunch at yours? Biscuit is already packing his bowl.
Red flowers in the window boxes. No idea of the name. Biscuit knows.
He walked me to the rosemary bush. He likes it. I like it too.
Dad, the lemon tree you gave me has six lemons. Six, Dad.
I'll send you a photo of the oleanders. Pink, white, pink.
Big day tomorrow. Trim the basil, then pesto, then a nap.
Biscuit remembers you. Say his name. See? Tail.
The church bell up the hill just rang. You can hear it? Nice.
I'm standing by the fountain. It smells of wet stone and roses.
He wants a lemon leaf to carry home. Fine. One leaf.
Remember the hammock under the apricot tree? I do, every evening.
Camille's geraniums are the tallest on the street. Don't tell.
Tonight's plan: the lantern walk, then cocoa. His is water.
Auntie wants a lemon from here. I'll post one. Wrapped nicely.
Yes, it's blue hour. The whole town goes soft, Mum. Like velvet.
Biscuit has sat down in the flower bed. Gently. Very gently.
He sneezed at the lavender. Then went back for more.
We'll plant the sunflower seeds tomorrow. Biscuit has the spot.
Remember your mother's roses? Same red as these. Exactly.
No, Mum, I'm not cold. Biscuit is lying on my feet.
The kiosk has peonies tonight. I'm bringing two home.

He's checking every planter on the way. Quality control.
Look, the first star. Over the cypress. Make a wish, Mum.
Yes, the lemon tree gets the morning sun. Like you said.

He just lay down under the orange tree. We live here now.
Dad says hello? Tell him the olive tree says hello back.
I'll call Grandma tomorrow at nine. She likes the dog part.

Biscuit and the bougainvillea. Both in their best colours.

Blue hour. The jasmine is loud tonight, if smells are loud.
Biscuit picked a petal for later. He keeps it in his mouth.
Mum, the lamps came on. One by one. Like a queue.

Hold on, Mum. Biscuit is interviewing a shutter.

He found a leaf. He is carrying it like a diploma.

Biscuit is sitting. On purpose. Write it down, Mum.

Sister, the tiles are still warm. Biscuit lies on every one.

Mum, I counted the shutters. Biscuit counted the smells.

The roofs went silver, Mum. Zinc does that at this hour.

Yes, the gulls are quieter now. Indoor voices.

Mum says hello to Biscuit. Biscuit says hello to a pebble.

The warm stone again. Every evening, same stone. He lies on it.

One more minute, Mum. He is finishing a sniff.
Biscuit tried to catch a reflection. A very wet hello.

The cat on the wall has a white sock. Just one. Stylish.
He is listening to the lights hum. Or my stomach.
The gulls are going to bed. The roof ones, at least.
Sister, the sea went silver. Biscuit sat down to look.
No, Mum, I will not let him phone you himself. Paws.

Sister, he has found a feather. He is wearing it, sort of.
Mum, that bell was the kiosk shutter. Not a cow.
Biscuit says a gull owes him a crumb. Old business.
Yes, Mum. Bed soon. After the long way round. His rule.
Look how the windows go gold one at a time. Like advent.
Blue hour. Biscuit is a slightly bluer Biscuit.
He sniffs each tile like it might be a different tile.
Shutters closing all down the street. Click, click, goodnight.
He has found a lamp he likes. We are staying a while.
Biscuit is walking me. I am happy to be walked.
One gull left on the railing. Biscuit says goodnight to it.
He stopped to admire a window box. Geraniums. Good taste.
A blue evening and a brown dog. That is the whole plan.
The fountain lion and Biscuit. Two heads, same thoughts.
Biscuit thinks the moon is a very far ball. Fair enough.
The palm trees rustle. Biscuit answers with one ear.
He has a favourite tile. Third from the fountain. Blue.

Mum, it's me. Biscuit sends a paw. Metaphorically.

The detective has a dog too. Biscuit is taking notes.

Camille asked after you, Mum. I said you were knitting.
Green wool, Mum? He approves. Green is his second favourite.

No, Mum, he's not spoiled. He's appreciated.
Video call, Biscuit. Look at Grandma. No, the phone. Here.

Marcel says bonsoir to you. Yes, with the bow.

Knight to somewhere. I'll text you when Biscuit decides.
I've started a little notebook of his walks. Page twelve.
Tonight's entry: three lamp posts, one fountain, one nice pigeon.

Too much cumin? Never. You taught me that.

Inès just jogged past and waved. Everyone waves here, Mum.

Lucie rang her bell for Biscuit. He did a little spin.
Mum, I found a secondhand book of poems. Sea ones.

Biscuit's ribbon is blue tonight. To match the sky.

Sister, play me the piano bit. Hold the phone closer.

Camille's little one drew Biscuit. Four legs and a sun.

Sister, the lights look like a necklace on the promenade.
